llm.summary: This is a coherent Gaode/AMap command-line mapping skill with expected API calls, but users should handle the API key and location data carefully.

dimensions.detail: Network access to https://restapi.amap.com and use of AMAP_API_KEY are proportionate to the stated mapping purpose. I found no subprocess execution, broad file access, local indexing, or hidden network destinations.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer or dependency setup performs automatic changes. Documentation includes an optional command to append AMAP_API_KEY to ~/.bashrc and many examples using --key, which are user-directed but can expose or persist the credential.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill clearly says it calls Gaode Web Service APIs, and commands are user-directed. It does not provide detailed per-command privacy notices, so users should understand that IPs, addresses, coordinates, routes, and search terms may be sent to Gaode/AMap.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no automatic persistence, privilege escalation, service installation, or backdoor behavior. The only persistence-like instruction is the documented optional shell profile entry for storing the API key.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The main script implements map-related functions matching the skill purpose: IP lookup, geocoding, reverse geocoding, POI search, route planning including transit, weather, traffic, and input tips. The older poi_search.py is narrower, but it remains map-related and does not add unrelated behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending map queries, addresses, coordinates, route endpoints, and IP-derived location data to Gaode/AMap. Prefer AMAP_API_KEY from a secure environment or secret store, avoid putting the key directly after --key in commands, restrict the key in the Gaode console where possible, and rotate it if it has been exposed in shell history or logs.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: gaode_map.py does implement the advertised all-in-one map capabilities except a separate bus command; transit routing is provided under route, and IP/reverse geocoding are documented in SKILL.md.
[YR4] expected: Downgraded: the matched content is AIGC metadata and a map description, not exploit tooling or tool-poisoning instructions.
[YR1] expected: Downgraded: the ~/.bashrc line is a documented optional way for a user to persist an API key environment variable, not an automatic or hidden backdoor.
[LP3] expected: Partly accepted as a governance note: the skill needs outbound AMap API access and AMAP_API_KEY, but those needs are disclosed in the documentation and are proportionate to the purpose.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted as user guidance rather than a Review-level issue: location and search inputs are sent to Gaode/AMap as expected for a map API, but the docs could be clearer about privacy at each command.
[SDI-4] expected: Accepted as a documentation mismatch only: poi_search.py and gaode_map.py have minor command/help inconsistencies, but they do not show hidden or unrelated behavior.
[SDI-1] expected: Accepted as low-impact scope drift: reverse geocoding and IP lookup are map functions and are documented in the skill body; the missing standalone bus command is not a security concern.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: mixed Chinese/English output is a usability limitation, not evidence of unsafe behavior.
[T09] expected: Accepted as a real credential-handling caution: command-line API keys can leak through shell history, logs, or process listings, although the key is only used for the expected AMap API calls.
